catalog.name: Root account MFA is off
catalog.why: The root user has full control of the account. Without MFA, a stolen password gives an attacker everything.
fix: Sign in as the root user
Open Security credentials
Add an authenticator or hardware MFA device
Store root credentials offline

catalog.name: IAM users without MFA
catalog.why: Console users without a second factor are exposed to password theft.
fix: Find users in the IAM credential report
Enforce MFA through a policy or move to SSO
Remove console access that is not needed

catalog.name: Access keys older than 90 days
catalog.why: Old keys are more likely to have leaked and are rarely rotated.
fix: Create a new key
Update the application to use it
Disable the old key, then delete it after a check period

catalog.name: Unused IAM users and roles
catalog.why: Dormant identities widen the attack surface and are rarely watched.
fix: Review last-used dates
Disable identities unused for 90 days
Delete them after confirmation

catalog.name: Weak password policy
catalog.why: Short or non-expiring passwords are easier to guess or reuse.
fix: Set a minimum length of 14
Require mixed characters and symbols
Prevent reuse of the last 5 passwords

catalog.name: Public S3 buckets
catalog.why: Public buckets are a leading cause of data exposure.
fix: Turn on Block Public Access at account level
Review bucket policies and ACLs
Serve intended public content through CloudFront

catalog.name: S3 buckets without encryption
catalog.why: Unencrypted objects miss encryption-at-rest expectations.
fix: Enable default encryption with SSE-KMS
Re-encrypt existing objects where needed

catalog.name: Security groups open to the internet on SSH or RDP
catalog.why: Remote admin ports open to 0.0.0.0/0 invite brute-force attacks.
fix: Restrict the source to known IP ranges
Use Session Manager instead of open ports
Remove the 0.0.0.0/0 rule

catalog.name: Unencrypted EBS volumes and databases
catalog.why: Data at rest is readable if a disk or snapshot is exposed.
fix: Turn on EBS encryption by default
Copy unencrypted volumes to encrypted ones
Restore databases from encrypted snapshots

catalog.name: CloudTrail is not enabled in all regions
catalog.why: Without full audit logs, activity cannot be traced after an incident.
fix: Create an organisation or multi-region trail
Send logs to a protected S3 bucket

catalog.name: Publicly accessible databases
catalog.why: A database reachable from the internet is open to direct attack.
fix: Set the database to not publicly accessible
Move it into private subnets
Allow access only from application security groups

catalog.name: Default VPC still in use
catalog.why: The default VPC has permissive defaults and is easy to misuse.
fix: Create purpose-built VPCs
Migrate workloads
Delete the default VPC once it is empty

catalog.name: CloudTrail log file validation is off
catalog.why: Without validation, tampering with logs is hard to detect.
fix: Enable log file validation on each trail

catalog.name: KMS key rotation is disabled
catalog.why: Keys that never rotate increase the impact of a key compromise.
fix: Enable automatic rotation on customer managed keys

catalog.name: VPC flow logs are disabled
catalog.why: Without network logs, suspicious traffic is hard to investigate.
fix: Enable flow logs to CloudWatch or S3
Set a retention period

catalog.name: AWS Config is not enabled
catalog.why: Without configuration history, changes and drift go unnoticed.
fix: Turn on AWS Config in each region in use
Record all supported resource types

catalog.name: S3 buckets accept non-HTTPS requests
catalog.why: Data in transit can be intercepted over plain HTTP.
fix: Add a bucket policy that denies requests when aws:SecureTransport is false

catalog.name: IAM policies with wildcard admin access
catalog.why: Full-access policies break least privilege and magnify any compromise.
fix: Find policies that allow all actions on all resources
Replace them with scoped permissions
Use IAM Access Analyzer to guide tightening

catalog.name: Log retention is too short
catalog.why: Log groups kept for less than the required minimum (90 days, or 365 days when HIPAA is in scope) leave gaps for investigations and audits.
fix: Set log group retention to at least 90 days, or 365 days when HIPAA is in scope
Archive older logs to S3

catalog.name: No budget alerts are set
catalog.why: Missing alerts let spending anomalies run unnoticed.
fix: Create a monthly budget
Add alerts at 80 and 100 percent

catalog.name: Root account has access keys
catalog.why: Access keys for the root user give unrestricted, long-lived access to the whole account.
fix: Sign in as the root user
Delete every root access key
Use IAM roles or SSO for programmatic access

catalog.name: EC2 instances do not require IMDSv2
catalog.why: Instances that still allow IMDSv1 can have their role credentials stolen through server-side request forgery.
fix: Set the instance metadata option HttpTokens to required
Set the account default to require IMDSv2
Check that applications use IMDSv2 first

catalog.name: EC2 instances without an IAM role
catalog.why: Instances without a role tend to use stored access keys, which are harder to protect and rotate.
fix: Create a role with only the permissions the workload needs
Attach it as the instance profile
Remove any access keys stored on the instance

catalog.name: DynamoDB tables without point-in-time recovery
catalog.why: Without point-in-time recovery, an accidental delete or bad write cannot be rolled back.
fix: Turn on point-in-time recovery for each table
Set a backup plan for tables that need longer retention

catalog.name: Lambda functions with wildcard permissions
catalog.why: A function role that can do everything turns any code flaw into full account access.
fix: Find the function's execution role
Replace administrator or wildcard policies with scoped permissions
Use IAM Access Analyzer to see which actions are actually used

catalog.name: Lambda function URLs without authentication
catalog.why: A function URL with no authentication can be called by anyone on the internet.
fix: Switch the URL auth type to AWS_IAM
Or put the function behind API Gateway with an authorizer
Delete URLs that are no longer needed

catalog.name: AWS Config does not record all resource types
catalog.why: A recorder that skips resource types leaves blind spots in change history and compliance checks.
fix: Edit the recorder
Choose to record all supported resource types

catalog.name: GuardDuty is not enabled
catalog.why: Without GuardDuty, suspicious activity such as credential misuse or crypto mining is not detected.
fix: Enable GuardDuty in each region in use
Send findings to an alert channel
Note that GuardDuty is a paid service with a free trial

catalog.name: GuardDuty has open high-severity findings
catalog.why: Unresolved high-severity findings indicate active or likely compromise.
fix: Open each finding in the GuardDuty console
Investigate and contain the affected resource
Archive the finding once resolved

catalog.name: Security Hub is not enabled
catalog.why: Security Hub gathers findings from several services and runs ongoing standards checks in one place.
fix: Enable Security Hub in each region in use
Choose the standards that apply
Note that Security Hub and AWS Config are paid services

catalog.name: Public entry points without a web application firewall
catalog.why: Internet-facing load balancers and CloudFront distributions without WAF are exposed to common web attacks.
fix: Create a web ACL with the AWS managed rule groups
Associate it with each public load balancer or distribution
Start in count mode to check for false positives
